decision_triggers: If line_loss_events is 0 on all tracks and max_error still sits at 0.060 m or above on the S-bend and slalom, record the course position of the peak error. This is the evidence that bend authority is the limit.
If line_loss_events returns on any track, report the position where it begins and the steering signal there. Do not change geometry.
If steering_oscillation rises well above the iteration 9 value of 0.23 on the oval, lower kp before touching geometry.
integration_questions: Does the current kp and kd hold the oval finish rate at 8 of 20 or better, with the same geometry as iteration 9?
At what course position does the largest S-bend and slalom max_error occur, and what is the steering signal there?
Is steering_oscillation on the oval in line with iteration 9 (0.23), or has the controller change moved it?

intent: Hold the iteration 9 geometry exactly, since it is the only design measured with zero line loss on every development track and the best score so far (209.98). The controller work the Integrator is doing is tuned to this platform, so the final race isolates that controller. Expected result: line_loss_events stays at 0 on the oval, S-bend and slalom, the oval finish rate holds at or above 8 of 20, and max_error on the S-bend and slalom stays near 0.060 m. No geometry change is made this iteration, because the one candidate lever (wheel_track 0.09 m) is untested and would also raise the effective steering gain.
learning: Iteration 9 is the first design with line loss cleared on every development track, so the span and mass are settled and the controller now sets the score. The untested wheel_track 0.09 m idea was not raced and was not carried forward, because this is the final iteration and no later race could confirm it. The open question for any future work is whether bend max_error falls with narrower track authority, or whether it rises only because the effective gain goes up.
rationale:
Iteration 9 is the best design so far (score 209.98). Its geometry (seven 16 mm sensors at x = -0.05 to +0.05 m, y = 0.04 m, mass 0.6 kg, wheel_track 0.10 m, wheel_radius 0.03 m, body 0.18 x 0.12 m) produced zero line-loss events on all three development tracks, and the oval finished 8 of 20 seeds. Its remaining limit is max_error: 0.0552 m on the oval, 0.0601 m on the S-bend and 0.0624 m on the slalom, against the fixed 0.06 m off-track limit. Body width cannot move that limit, and mass from 0.7 to 0.6 kg changed max_error by under 0.002 m, so neither is a lever.

The one geometry lever with a physical basis is wheel_track. The contract defines turn rate as the wheel speed difference divided by wheel_track, so a narrower track gives more yaw per PWM difference. Iteration 10 proposed 0.09 m for that reason. It was never raced, though, and the Integrator tuned the controller on the 0.10 m track. Narrowing raises the effective steering gain by about 11 percent, so it could bring back the oscillation or line loss that iteration 9 just cleared, and the 0.06 m limit might not improve. This is also the final iteration, and the final unseen-track race is scored with no later correction. A change I cannot test, on a track that was tuned for 0.10 m, is a poor risk. I therefore hold every geometry value at the iteration 9 design. That keeps the best-measured platform for the controller already tuned on it and gives the final race the most reliable base. The narrower-track test is recorded as an open hypothesis in the feedback request.

Expected result: a score close to iteration 9 (about 200 or more), with line_loss_events staying at 0 on all tracks. The measurements requested will show whether the bend max_error is still near 0.06 m, which would be the evidence needed for the wheel_track test in any later work.
